newsitem.title: BRAZIL: New Brazil wheat scheme sees low first sales.
newsitem.headline: New Brazil wheat scheme sees low first sales.

text.p: The first auction of Brazilian wheat in a new scheme devised by the government to ensure farmers receive the minimum price resulted in the sale of only 4.86 percent of the wheat offered, a bank spokesman said.
Only 4,859 tonnes of the 100,000 tonnes included in today's auction was bought, said the spokesman from Banco do Brasil, which held the electronic sale.
The auction is designed to set not outright prices but the level of the subsidies to be paid by the government.
The buyer then pays the government the minimum price of 157 reais ($152.43) minus the subsidy while the government pays the farmer the full 157 reais.
At today's sale, the maximum subsidy was 49 reais ($47.57) and the minimum 14 reais ($13.59).
Most of the wheat bought today was from Parana which accounted for 3,527 tonnes. The remaining wheat was from Rio Grande do Sul (1,224 tonnes) and Santa Catarina (108).
The largest individual purchase was for 2,500 tonnes of Parana wheat to be delivered to Rio Janeiro or Espirito Santo states.
A second auction of 100,000 tonnes is scheduled to be held on November 22.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
